A 16-year-old male presents for a preparticipation physical evaluation for high school basketball. He is
asymptomatic, with no limitations in physical activity, abnormal growth, or development. His family
history is notable for a younger brother diagnosed with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) during evaluation of
an innocent murmur, but there is no history of heart disease, sudden cardiac death, or unexplained
death in other family members. On examination, his heart rate is 72 beats per minute, oxygen
saturation is 98%, and blood pressure is 106/77 mm Hg in the right upper extremity and 128/76 mm Hg
in the right lower extremity. His height is 183 cm (90th percentile), weight is 59 kg (41st percentile), and
BMI is 23.6. Physical examination reveals a regular heart rate and rhythm with no murmur, click, or
gallop. Brachial and femoral pulses are 2+ bilaterally without brachiofemoral delay. What is the most
appropriate next step for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Obtain cardiac MRI (B) Schedule follow-up
in 6 months (C) Obtain chest X-ray (D) Clear for all sports participation without further testing (E)
Obtain an echocardiogram (F) Monitor blood pressure for 24 hours (G) Refer to pediatric cardiologist
(H) Restrict from competitive sports (I) Perform exercise stress test (J) Obtain a cardiac CT angiogram
 A. Clear for all sports participation without further testing
B. Monitor blood pressure for 24 hours
C. Perform exercise stress test
D. Obtain a cardiac CT angiogram
E. Obtain an echocardiogram
F. Obtain chest X-ray
G. Restrict from competitive sports
H. Refer to pediatric cardiologist
I. Obtain cardiac MRI
J. Schedule follow-up in 6 months
